title: Selenium + TestNG UI automation framework
summary: Build a maintainable web UI framework in Java: Page Object Model, explicit waits, a WebDriver factory that runs headless in CI, TestNG groups for smoke and regression, data-driven tests and screenshots on failure. Start from the runnable example in the repo and extend it against a practice site of your choice.

title: RestAssured API regression suite
summary: Write an API test suite in Java with RestAssured: request and response specifications, JSON schema validation, CRUD flows that create and clean up their own data, negative tests for status codes and error bodies, and auth handled once in a shared spec. The repo ships a runnable starting point.

title: JMeter load-test suite with reporting
summary: Design a load test for a public demo API or a local app: model realistic user journeys with thread groups, correlate dynamic values with extractors, parameterise data from CSV, add assertions, run in non-GUI mode and publish the HTML dashboard. Write a short report stating the workload model, the results and what limited throughput.

title: Playwright end-to-end suite in TypeScript
summary: Cover a real web app's critical journeys with Playwright Test: fixtures for logged-in state, web-first assertions instead of sleeps, API calls to seed data, cross-browser projects, trace and video on retry, and a small set of visual or accessibility checks. Keep the suite fast enough to run on every pull request.

title: CI pipeline that runs and reports your tests
summary: Take one of your test projects and wire it into GitHub Actions (or another CI): run unit, API and UI stages in sensible order, cache dependencies, shard slow suites, publish JUnit and HTML reports as artifacts, and fail the build on real regressions while quarantining known flaky tests with a tracked reason.

title: Appium mobile automation for an Android app
summary: Automate an open-source Android app with Appium: set up an emulator, choose stable locators (accessibility ids over XPath), handle permissions, gestures and app state resets, and structure screens as page objects. Document which device and OS versions you tested and what you could not automate.

title: SQL data validation for an ETL pipeline
summary: Load a public dataset into a staging table, transform it into a reporting table, then write SQL checks that prove the load is correct: row-count reconciliation, null and duplicate checks on keys, referential integrity, range and format rules, and source-to-target comparisons of aggregates. Automate the checks with pytest so they run after every load.

title: Evaluation harness for an LLM feature
summary: Build a repeatable evaluation for an LLM-powered feature such as a summariser or a small RAG chatbot: a versioned golden dataset, deterministic checks (format, refusal, required facts), rubric-based grading with documented limits, regression comparison between prompt versions, and a set of adversarial prompts for prompt injection and hallucination.

title: Test plan and test cases for a real web app
summary: Pick a public web app and produce the artefacts a manual QA hands over: a one-page test plan with scope and risks, requirement-traced test cases using boundary values and equivalence partitions, an exploratory session charter with notes, and well-written bug reports with clear reproduction steps.

title: RAG chatbot with an evaluation suite
summary: Build a question-answering chatbot over a public documentation set: ingestion, chunking, embeddings, vector search, cited answers and a refusal when the context lacks the answer. Create a labelled question set and measure retrieval recall at k separately from answer faithfulness and correctness, then compare two chunking strategies with the numbers.

title: LLM evaluation harness that gates CI
summary: Write a Python harness that runs a versioned evaluation set against a prompt and model configuration, scores outputs with deterministic checks and a rubric-based LLM judge calibrated against your own hand labels, compares results with a stored baseline per category, and fails the CI pipeline when quality drops below agreed thresholds. Repeat runs to measure variance and document what the harness cannot detect.

title: Prompt-injection red-team suite for your own LLM app
summary: Build a small LLM app you own, such as an assistant that reads documents and can call one harmless tool, then write an automated suite of direct and indirect prompt-injection, system-prompt extraction and data-leakage cases. Check actual side effects such as tool calls, apply defences like least privilege and confirmation, and rerun to show which attacks they stop. Only test systems you own or are authorised to test.

title: ML model training, experiment tracking and drift monitoring
summary: Train a baseline and an improved model on a public tabular dataset with correct, leakage-free splits, track every run's parameters, data version and metrics in an experiment tracker, register the best model, serve it behind an API in a container, and monitor feature and prediction drift against the training reference with an alert when a simulated shift occurs.
